title: Time to DOUBLE UP on Amazon?
creator: Mark Roussin CPA
source_note: Detailed summary generated from video captions; auto-captions garble names/numbers in places
summary: Mark Roussin CPA weighs doubling up on Amazon after third-quarter results that have him seriously considering adding more, then compares Amazon with Alphabet, his other large position, to decide where his next dollar goes. Amazon's revenue grew 12% year on year to over $200 billion in a quarter — without Prime Day, which moved to the second quarter this year versus the third last year — while operating income jumped about 61%, from $17.4 billion to $28.1 billion, for a record roughly 14% operating margin, the highest in company history. He credits prior investment cycles: Amazon has repeatedly spent heavily (e-commerce, delivery speed, cloud, now AI) and each time it has paid off. AWS is accelerating, with revenue up 39% year on year and growth guided above 40% into 2027-28, and custom Trainium chips plus inference growth add a new profit pool. Valuation looks cheap on his measures: forward PE 24x versus a five-year average of 46x, and forward EV/EBITDA near 10x, close to historic lows. The bear case is cash: free cash flow is deeply negative (about -$47 billion trailing twelve months) with roughly $220 billion of capex this year rising into 2027, so if AI spend does not pay off, valuation compresses. Alphabet, by contrast, is not being sold — it remains his largest holding — but ad revenue missed expectations for a second straight quarter, so Amazon gets his next dollar. Calls: AMZN — BUY (reiterated from 13 October), GOOGL — HOLD (reiterated from 29 October).
